title: Yanwan Zhu
text:
Hi! I’m a sixth year PhD student in the Department of Cognitive and Psychological Sciences at Brown University. I’m advised by Roman Feiman and affiliated with the BLT lab. Here is the most updated version my CV.
About my name: To pronounce my last name semi-accurately (i.e. enough to make me realize that I am being referred to), you could say juice without the [s]. For the phonetics enthusiasts, here is my full name in IPA: [jɛnwan ʈʂu]

title: Research
text:
Overview
My research interests lie at the intersection of many branches of cognitive science, including but not limited to: developmental psychology, semantics & pragmatics, philosophy of mind, etc. Below is a list of projects I have worked on, organized by topics.


Acquisition of possibility concept and language
The main focus of my PhD work has been on children’s concept of possibility — the ability to mark a proposition as being merely possible (like the operator \(\Diamond\) in modal logic). I ask: can this logical concept be learned without language, or do they have to be constructed through the process of figuring out what words and phrases mean in a language?

Yanwan Zhu & Roman Feiman. Toddlers use “if”, rather than “when”, to talk about mere possibilities.





Language acquisition in understudied populations
When I was an undergrad at Smith College, I worked with Jill de Villiers on a project focusing on Romani-speaking children in Europe. In our paper, in addition to presenting data on Roma children’s linguistic knowledge, we argued that studying language acquisition in understudied populations like Roma children is important, highlighting both the scientific merits and the societal implications.
